Dearest Traveler,

Shikoku is the island of the long road, where the dust of the path is a sacred blessing. For over twelve centuries, pilgrims dressed in white have walked the 1,200-kilometer road connecting eighty-eight holy temples. To walk Shikoku is to learn that the destination is merely an excuse for the journey itself.

Away from the pilgrimage paths, the ancient hot waters of Dogo Onsen steam under wooden eaves, healing the tired bones of kings and commoners alike. And the Iya Valley hides rope bridges woven from living vines over rushing turquoise rivers. Shikoku teaches us that our paths may be long and winding, but every step is a home.

With every step of the journey,
Kokoro of Shikoku
